उत्तर प्रदेश में फिर बढ़ेगा तापमान, पश्चिमी यूपी में बारिश के आसार (Ai Image)
UP Weather Update: यूपी में मौसम बदलने वाला है. पश्चिमी यूपी में कुछ जगहों पर बारिश हो सकती है, जबकि तापमान बढ़ने से गर्मी का एहसास होगा. जानें IMD का पूर्वानुमान.
UP Weather Update: उत्तर प्रदेश में आने वाले दिनों में मौसम में बदलाव देखने को मिल सकता है. भारतीय मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) के ताजा पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश के कुछ हिस्सों में हल्की बारिश होने की संभावना है. वहीं, पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में मौसम मुख्य रूप से शुष्क बना रह सकता है। विभाग के अनुसार, अगले कुछ दिनों में प्रदेश के कई इलाकों में तापमान बढ़ने के आसार हैं. ऐसे में लोगों को दिन के समय फिर से गर्मी का एहसास हो सकता है.
पश्चिमी यूपी में इन तारीखों पर बारिश के आसार
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश के कुछ जिलों में 11 अक्टूबर को हल्की बारिश हो सकती है. इसके अलावा 14, 15 और 16 अक्टूबर को भी कुछ स्थानों पर छिटपुट बारिश होने की संभावना जताई गई है. हालांकि, 10, 12 और 13 अक्टूबर को पश्चिमी यूपी में मौसम सामान्य रूप से शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है. बारिश की गतिविधियां सीमित रहने के कारण तापमान में बढ़ोतरी हो सकती है. ऐसे में लोगों को दिन के समय गर्मी का सामना करना पड़ सकता है.
पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में फिलहाल बारिश की संभावना कम
पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश के जिलों में अगले कुछ दिनों तक मौसम साफ और शुष्क रहने की संभावना है. मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक, 10 अक्टूबर से 16 अक्टूबर तक पूर्वी यूपी में बारिश को लेकर कोई विशेष संभावना नहीं जताई गई है. इस दौरान आसमान में स्थानीय स्तर पर बादल दिखाई दे सकते हैं, लेकिन व्यापक बारिश का अनुमान नहीं है. मौसम के शुष्क रहने के साथ ही तापमान में भी बढ़ोतरी होने के आसार हैं. इससे दिन में गर्मी बढ़ सकती है, जबकि मौसम में ठंडक का इंतजार जारी रहेगा.
वायुमंडलीय गतिविधियों का मौसम पर पड़ सकता है असर
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश और आसपास के क्षेत्रों में निचले वायुमंडल में चक्रवाती परिसंचरण बना हुआ है. इसके साथ ही उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत में पश्चिमी विक्षोभ और अन्य मौसमी गतिविधियां आसपास के राज्यों के मौसम को प्रभावित कर सकती हैं. उत्तराखंड, हरियाणा, चंडीगढ़ और दिल्ली के कुछ इलाकों में छिटपुट बारिश या हवाओं की गतिविधि देखने को मिल सकती है. इन मौसमी परिस्थितियों का आंशिक असर पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश के कुछ जिलों में भी पड़ने की संभावना है.
मानसून की वापसी के बीच तापमान बढ़ने के संकेत
देश के विभिन्न हिस्सों से दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून की वापसी के लिए परिस्थितियां अनुकूल बनी हुई हैं. मानसून की विदाई के इस दौर में उत्तर प्रदेश के मौसम में भी बदलाव देखने को मिल रहा है. विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, प्रदेश के पूर्वी हिस्सों में फिलहाल बारिश की गतिविधियां सीमित रहेंगी, जबकि पश्चिमी यूपी में कुछ दिनों पर हल्की बारिश हो सकती है. आने वाले दिनों में तापमान बढ़ने की संभावना है. ऐसे में लोगों को मौसम के ताजा अपडेट पर नजर रखनी चाहिए और बदलते मौसम के अनुसार अपनी दिनचर्या तय करनी चाहिए.

Bhaskar AnalysisGujarat sees rise in hot days and warm nights:IMD study finds 2.3 more hot days and 11.5 more warm nights every decade
- Copy link
Gujarat has been witnessing a sustained rise in extreme temperatures, with the number of days recording temperatures above 35°C increasing by 2.3 days and nights with temperatures above 20°C rising by 1.5 nights every decade.
The findings emerged from an extensive study of daily temperature data from 1951 to 2025 conducted by scientists from the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The research, which examines climate trends across India and Gujarat, has been published in the International Journal of Climatology.
The rising temperatures are putting increasing pressure on agriculture, particularly due to the accumulation of heat units during the cotton-growing season. The trend signals a growing challenge for the state's agricultural sector.
The study analyses the country's agro-climatic zones rather than individual states. Gujarat falls mainly under two zones: Gujarat Plains and Hills (ACZ-13) and the adjoining Western Dry Region (ACZ-14).
Gujarat and Western Dry Region Emerge as Major Heat Hotspots
Both daytime and night-time temperatures are rising in Gujarat and the Western Dry Region. The latter has emerged as the country's largest thermal hotspot, with hot nights increasing at the fastest rate nationally. The gap between daytime and night-time temperatures is also narrowing rapidly.
In northern India, particularly the Gangetic Plains, extensive irrigation has helped limit the rise in daytime temperatures, while nights have become warmer.
Southern and coastal regions show the opposite pattern, with daytime temperatures rising faster than night-time temperatures.
Warmer Nights Pose Risks to Livestock and Dairy Industry
Persistently high night-time temperatures threaten livestock as well as crops. When nights remain warm, animals get less opportunity to dissipate the heat accumulated during the day.
This heat stress can adversely affect their reproductive capacity, raising concerns for livestock farming and the dairy industry.

The India Meteorological Department has issued a heatwave warning for isolated parts of Mumbai and Raigad, with hot and humid conditions expected across sections of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and the Konkan belt until October 12. The warning follows the withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from Maharashtra and a forecast rise in temperatures over the next few days.
The Regional Meteorological Centre in Mumbai said isolated pockets of Mumbai and Raigad were likely to experience heatwave conditions on Friday, October 9. It also forecast hot and humid weather at isolated locations in North Konkan, while parts of South Konkan could experience heatwave conditions.
The IMD expects maximum temperatures to rise by 2 to 3 degrees Celsius in some parts of Maharashtra over the next 48 hours. Temperatures could increase by another 1 to 3 degrees Celsius thereafter, according to the weather information cited in the report. Maximum temperatures in parts of interior Maharashtra are likely to remain between 37 and 39 degrees Celsius on October 9 and 10.
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region includes Mumbai and adjoining areas in Thane, Palghar and Raigad districts. The urban agglomeration extends across nine municipal corporations, meaning that a regional weather warning can affect residents, commuters and outdoor workers across multiple municipal jurisdictions even when conditions vary between locations.
The alert is the first heatwave warning issued for Mumbai and some other parts of Maharashtra in the current episode, according to the report. The expected combination of high temperatures and humidity could increase discomfort, particularly in areas where hot conditions persist through the day. The IMD has distinguished between the expected conditions in different parts of the Konkan region rather than issuing a uniform forecast for the entire coastal belt.
Residents have been advised to follow official weather updates, drink sufficient water and limit prolonged exposure to direct sunlight during the hottest part of the day. These precautions are particularly relevant for people who work outdoors, travel during peak afternoon hours or live in neighbourhoods with limited access to shaded public spaces and cooling facilities.
The weather department has also forecast light rain and thundershowers in parts of southern Maharashtra during the afternoon or evening over the weekend. The IMD’s warning for the Mumbai region and Konkan remains in force until October 12, with local conditions expected to vary across districts and isolated pockets.

Nagpur: What would Rs 41.09 lakh buy in Nagpur? A 580sqft flat in Friends Colony. But state PWD plans to spend almost the same amount to renovate the dining area and a general toilet at a govt bungalow in Civil Lines. The fresh spending comes amid Maharashtra’s severe drought crisis and the state PWD’s substantial financial liabilities.
The work is part of three fresh tenders of Rs10.11cr combined floated by PWD Division No. 1 on Thursday, barely a day after questions were raised over its earlier Rs10.38cr fund splurge for 94 pre-winter session repair work.
The fresh tenders cover 57 works — 26 works of Rs 4.77cr in one package, 24 works worth Rs 3.5cr in another and seven works of Rs1.84cr in the third. All works carry a one-month completion period, indicating the urgency with which the department wants to complete them ahead of Maharashtra legislature’s winter session in Nagpur in December.
The most striking expenditure is at Bungalow 27/1 in Civil Lines, where PWD proposed Rs41.6 lakh for strengthening the meeting hall and other repairs and another Rs 41.09 lakh for renovating the dining area and general toilet.
Together, the two works cost Rs 82.69 lakh. The Rs 41.09-lakh estimate for a dining area and toilet is particularly striking when compared with prevailing residential property prices.
The fresh tenders also include Rs 42.02 lakh for strengthening a roadside passage with stamped concrete at Ramgiri Bungalow and another Rs 42.02 lakh for replacement of roof and renovation of Ministerial Cottage No.13 at Ravi Bhavan.
A close look at tender documents shows several other high-value renovations at premises used during the winter session. At Vidhan Bhavan, PWD proposed Rs 82.78 lakh for two renovation works — Rs 41.6 lakh for the CM chamber, ante-chamber, dining room and washroom, and Rs 41.18 lakh for the CM office and toilet at the Old Annexe building.
At Hyderabad House, four works include Rs 21.1 lakh for internal and external painting of the new building. At MLA Hostel, Rs 38.66 lakh has been earmarked for external and oil painting of Wing No. 2 and Rs 23.53 lakh for Wings 3 and 4. At Deogiri, three works include repairs to ministerial cottages and PA quarters.
Several estimates also follow recurring slabs. Notice 49 includes two works pegged at Rs16.88 lakh each and two at Rs12.66 lakh. Other individual works carry estimates of Rs 21.1 lakh, Rs15.61 lakh, Rs15.19 lakh and Rs9.16 lakh.
A senior PWD official had earlier told TOI that repeated estimates are a result of the department’s standard maintenance-estimation process. For maintenance works below Rs10 lakh, detailed estimates are prepared after accounting for GST and other overheads, after which the amount is reflected in the technical sanction.
The official had also said the model code of conduct for the Nagpur Division Graduates’ Constituency election does not bar maintenance and RAC works in existing govt buildings.
Citizen Anil Wadpalliwar questioned the expenditure, saying, “When PWD is already struggling with around Rs17,000 crore in pending dues, it is legitimate to ask why it is taking on such additional repair expenditure. There should be an independent third-party audit and inspection to establish whether these works are genuinely necessary and justified.”
The spending also comes when Nagpur has a proposed Rs952-crore barrage on the Kanhan river to augment the city’s water storage capacity, with the proposal awaiting administrative approval.

Mumbai is likely to remain hot and humid on Saturday after the Santacruz observatory recorded 37.8°C on Friday, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to retain its yellow heatwave alert for Mumbai and Thane and issue a warning for hot and humid conditions at isolated places.
Friday’s maximum at Santacruz, the benchmark weather station for Mumbai, was 4.7°C above normal and slightly higher than Thursday’s 37.6°C. The city has recorded three of the 10 highest October temperatures at the station in the past seven days: 37.4°C on October 3, 37.6°C on October 8 and 37.8°C on October 9.
The Colaba observatory recorded a maximum of 37°C, which was 4.4°C above normal and among its highest October readings since 2014. Relative humidity reached 81% at Colaba and 73% at Santacruz, increasing the discomfort associated with the high temperatures.
The IMD attributed the spike to an anticyclone over Mumbai and neighbouring areas. The circulation pattern has stalled the sea breeze that normally brings relief to the city’s coastal areas. IMD scientist Sushma Nair said the system was well organised and that clear, cloudless skies had further contributed to the rise in temperatures.
“An anticyclone is a circulation pattern that causes air to sink towards the ground. The system over Mumbai is well organised, and clear, cloudless skies have further contributed to the rise in temperatures,” Nair said, according to the IMD explanation reported by the Times of India. She said the system was expected to become less organised and shift slightly on Saturday, which could bring some relief.
The weather pattern has affected the wider Konkan region, where several locations recorded temperatures between 38°C and 39°C. EL CENTRO — Extreme heat across Imperial County triggered nearly 300 heat-related illnesses and claimed 14 lives between mid-March and mid-September 2026, according to official surveillance data published by the Imperial County Public Health Department.
The agency’s seasonal Heat-related Illness Surveillance report—conducted annually in collaboration with El Centro Regional Medical Center (ECRMC), Pioneers Memorial Hospital (PMH), and the Imperial County Sheriff’s Coroner Division—monitors emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and fatalities tied to environmental heat exposure.
Between March 12 and Sept. 17, 2026, health officials tracked 292 cumulative cases of heat-related conditions. The total includes 144 cases of heat exhaustion, 118 cases categorized as other heat-related illnesses, 16 instances of severe heat stroke, and 14 deaths.
Of the total cases, 278 involved emergency department visits, resulting in 34 inpatient hospitalizations. The breakdown of hospital admissions shows 17 cases of heat exhaustion, 10 cases of heat stroke, and 7 cases of other heat illnesses. Among all cases with known age data ($n=278$), patients ranged from 4 to 97 years old, with a median age of 47.
Working-age adults bore the highest burden of severe exposure. Individuals aged 18 to 49 accounted for 48.63% of all cases, followed by those aged 50 to 64 at 26.03% and seniors aged 65 and older at 21.23%. Children and teenagers aged 0 to 17 represented 3.77% of cases, while unknown ages accounted for 0.34%.
Weekly case tracking highlighted a direct correlation between soaring local temperatures and spikes in medical emergencies. Peaks in reported cases occurred in July as weekly high temperatures hit 118°F and 116°F, before maintaining sustained elevated levels through August and September under temperatures ranging from 108°F to 116°F.

THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Rain is expected to continue across Kerala for the next five days, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). A yellow alert has been issued for four districts — Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki and Ernakulam — where isolated heavy rainfall is forecast.
Heavy rainfall refers to precipitation ranging from 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm within 24 hours. The IMD has advised people to follow safety precautions as strong winds and thunderstorms are also likely to accompany the rain.
A cyclonic circulation persists over the Gulf of Mannar and the adjoining coastal areas of southern Tamil Nadu at an altitude of 0.9 km above mean sea level. A low-pressure trough extending from this circulation towards north-central Maharashtra passes through interior Tamil Nadu and interior Karnataka. The IMD has also forecast the possibility of a low-pressure area developing over the Bay of Bengal.
Another cyclonic circulation over the Strait of Malacca is expected to move into the Andaman Sea on Sunday. It is likely to intensify into a low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal by October 13.
Isolated places in Kerala and Lakshadweep are likely to receive thundershowers accompanied by strong winds reaching speeds of 40–50 kmph on Saturday and Sunday, the IMD warned. Isolated thunderstorms and rain are also likely in Kerala from October 12 to 14, the weather department said.
